content.text: The first orientation was the right one, so I'm going back to it and making the nut thicker.
Good enough fit (IoU ≈ 0.977 — the rest is edge-line anti-aliasing). Exporting.

The part is a hex nut, built in `part.FCStd` and exported to `submission.step`. The exported file was read back and matches the part: one valid solid.

**Shape:**
- **Axis along X:** the hole runs along X, and the part is 11.5 mm thick in that direction.
- **Hexagon:** 20 mm across the flats, which run along Z, so it measures 23.09 mm corner to corner along Y.
- **Hole:** a plain through-hole, 12.5 mm in diameter.

**Fit to the reference:** the mean silhouette match is 0.977 across all four views (each view scored between 0.977 and 0.978). I got there in four tries:
- I tried turning the hexagon 30°, but the score dropped to 0.84, so I kept the first orientation.
- I adjusted the thickness: 12 mm and 11.5 mm scored the same, 13 mm was too thick, and 9 mm too thin.

The remaining differences are thin red lines along the outer edges of the diff image, mostly edge rendering rather than a difference in shape.

The silhouette comparison can't see the hole size, so 12.5 mm is my estimate from how large the hole looks in the views. That is the measurement most likely to be off in the voxel scoring.
